current.text: The projected OKC starters are Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Cason Wallace, Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein. The only open starting question is Ajay Mitchell in place of Wallace.
The experts expect him to come off the bench behind Wallace and Mitchell. Josh sees no chance he starts, even though ESPN lineup graphics show him starting.
OKC lost Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe this offseason. Ajay Mitchell, Cason Wallace and Nikola Topic also compete for guard minutes.
With those players gone, OKC will have to give more minutes to Mitchell and McCain.
He projects for about 2 to 2.5 threes and 12 points per game.
The experts call him overrated and pass on him at a Yahoo ADP of 100 to 112 (round 10 to 11). He is a flyer for deep leagues only.
He has his first fully healthy offseason and a stable role after a hard stint in Philadelphia and a midseason trade.
OKC values him more than outsiders do. The team believes in his on-ball ability to get to the rim, though he did not finish well there last season.
OKC lost its main shooters and could be one of the lowest three-point volume teams unless players like McCain shoot more.
OKC is projected for about 62 wins and a top-two seed in the West.
OKC has a league-minimum 13 back-to-backs. Its schedule is pretty good with a March 28 end date.

durable.text: He gives almost nothing except scoring and threes. He adds few rebounds, assists, steals, blocks or free throws, and his field goal shooting is not great.
He needs a lot of usage to matter for fantasy.
His output swings a lot. He has bright games but also games where he disappears, such as zero points in 10 minutes.

note: At Yahoo rank 171 and ESPN rank 232, with average costs of 1.0 USD and 0.2 USD, he falls outside the 144 players drafted in our league. The experts say pass even at his Yahoo ADP of about 100 to 112. He only adds threes (about 2.1 projected) and some points, so he is a waiver option for teams chasing 3PM, not a draft target. Early in the season, check whether his minutes climb clearly above last season's 17.4 toward ESPN's projected 24.7, and whether he passes Wallace or Mitchell in the guard rotation.
